statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 7, low, for the 03:00Z hour, down from 9. Nasdaq-100 futures are 29,358.50, down 29.25 points and 0.10%, at 02:55Z, back in the middle of a 29,301.25-29,470.25 overnight band after the second test of the low near 29,310.50 was bought. Both edges of the band have now been faded at least once and both directions have retraced, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path Tail measures, so Tail eases. S&P 500 futures are near flat and the Dow contract is unchanged, so the earlier drag stayed tech-specific. Stress is 38, moderate, down from 40: VIX finished Friday at 14.89, down 6.00%, crude is roughly 1.3% lower with WTI near $85.68 and Brent near $93.09 on profit-taking before the US sanctions announcement, and Treasury futures are modestly bid. Offsetting that, the 30-year yield sits near 5.276%, close to a 19-year peak, gold is near $4,623 after a 14% August gain, and Canada announced dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs from 8 September. Confidence is 85, high. The danger window remains 18:00Z-20:00Z for the Treasury press conference on new Iran sanctions.
recommendation: The overnight price path has completed a second full rotation rather than developing a trend. Nasdaq-100 futures printed 29,480.25, sold to 29,303.50, recovered to 29,430.25, returned to 29,310.50 and are 29,358.50 at 02:55Z, so both edges of a roughly 179-point band have been visited twice and faded twice. There is no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement, and no holding near a session extreme, which is why Tail steps down from 9 to 7 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. Cross-asset alignment is absent rather than confirming: oil is lower on pre-announcement profit-taking, gold is higher, Treasury futures are modestly bid, VIX is below 15, and S&P 500 futures are flat while the Nasdaq contract is marginally lower. That mixture argues for continued two-way behaviour, not directional efficiency. The identifiable risks in this window are scheduled rather than observed. The Treasury press conference on new Iran sanctions at 18:00Z is the one credible geopolitical discontinuity of the day, and the danger window is held narrow at 18:00Z-20:00Z rather than extended across the session; conditional Tail peaks at 19 there, still below the block threshold, because event importance and surprise magnitude raise Stress before they establish a pathological price path. Nvidia's results on 26 August and Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on 28 August sit outside this horizon but damp conviction inside it. Structure that would change the assessment is specific: an opening auction that extends with shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after a failed retracement, or futures holding a session extreme while yields, oil, semiconductors and breadth align in the same direction.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures return to mid-band at 29,358.50, down 0.10%, after a second low retest is bought: Tail eases to 7, low, mapped policy state EA_ON, with conditional readings of 7 to 19 across the next twenty-three hours.
body:
Five and a half hours into the Globex week the Nasdaq-100 has completed two full rotations of its overnight band and finished neither of them at an extreme. Futures topped at 29,480.25, sold to 29,303.50, recovered to 29,430.25 at 01:13Z, returned to 29,310.50 at 02:02Z and are 29,358.50, down 29.25 points and 0.10%, at 02:55Z on Investing.com, with Yahoo Finance showing 29,366.00 at 02:32Z. Against the 29,387.75 previous close that is a marginal net decline inside a band roughly 179 points wide. The important detail for a mean-reversion exposure is not the level but the shape: both edges have now been tested and both tests have been faded. That is the direct opposite of the persistent no-retracement path Tail is built to measure, and it is why Tail steps back from 9 to 7.

The tech-specific drag identified in the previous hour has not broadened. Samsung Electronics fell around 8% in Korean trading after a $79 billion shareholder-return package disappointed investors who had expected more given AI-driven profits, and analysts noted the absence of buyback detail. That weighed on Korean tech, but S&P 500 futures are near flat, the Dow contract is unchanged, and Asian equities overall are described as flat, with the Nikkei 225 at 66,092.05, up 0.11%. Idiosyncratic single-stock disappointment has stayed idiosyncratic.

Cross-asset evidence is mixed rather than aligned, which historically raises Stress and lowers conviction without raising Tail. VIX closed Friday at 14.89, down 6.00% on the day and comfortably below 15. Crude is roughly 1.3% lower, with WTI near $85.68 and Brent near $93.09, as investors take profits after a sharp weekly rally and ahead of the sanctions announcement. Treasury futures are modestly bid across the curve. Against that, the 30-year yield sits near 5.276%, within a whisker of its 19-year peak at 5.3371%, gold is near $4,623 after a gain of more than 14% in August, and Canada announced dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on US steel, electronics, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment and pulp and paper effective 8 September after trade talks failed. The last cash session left megacaps split five to three with unusually wide dispersion and semiconductors soft, so breadth confirms nothing in either direction. Stress therefore eases only modestly, from 40 to 38.

The day's identifiable risk is scheduled. Treasury Secretary Bessent holds a press conference at 18:00Z, or 2 p.m. Eastern, to announce what has been trailed as the toughest sanctions programme ever imposed on Iran, with explicit warnings to third countries that continue trading with Tehran. Energy is the obvious first transmission channel, and a genuine geopolitical discontinuity with a delayed second leg is the credible conditional path into equities. The danger window is held narrow at 18:00Z-20:00Z rather than extended across the session, and conditional Tail peaks at 19 in that hour, below the block threshold, because a scheduled and heavily trailed announcement is a checkpoint until an observed price path says otherwise.

Inside the forecast horizon the conditional path is unremarkable. Tail holds 7 to 9 through the remaining Asian hours and the European morning, steps to 10 for the 12:30Z Chicago Fed National Activity Index, and reaches 15 for the US cash open at 13:30Z, where opening-auction continuation is the most common source of the structure this exposure is vulnerable to. It then decays through the US morning and lunchtime before the sanctions window, and returns to single digits after the 20:00Z close. Nvidia's results on 26 August, with consensus near $92 billion of quarterly revenue, and Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on 28 August both sit beyond this horizon but keep conviction contained within it.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past twenty-four hours is nearly complete: twenty hourly assessments are available and four clock-hours are marked unavailable, at 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z on 23 August. Tail held 4 through every hour of the weekend futures halt, when no Nasdaq-100 price path could develop at all, stepped to 15 in the 22:00Z reopen hour to cover the still-unpriced weekend queue, then fell back to 9 at 23:00Z, 8 at 00:00Z and 7 at 01:00Z once the reopen printed without a gap and produced a complete round trip, before a small rise to 9 at 02:00Z on the second test of the session low. The mapped policy state stayed EA_ON and the dominant mode remained normal in every available hour, so no hour approached the block threshold. Stress traced a full weekend arc: 36 at the start of the window, a low of 34 through the European morning, then a steady climb through the US afternoon and evening to a peak of 45 at 21:00Z and 22:00Z as the reopen and the sanctions calendar approached, followed by a decline to 42, 39 and 38 once trade resumed in orderly fashion, and a small rebound to 40 at 02:00Z. Confidence ranged from 82 to 87, dipping in the reopen hour when live price evidence was thinnest and recovering to 86 once continuous quotes returned.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail 7 and Stress 38 on observed structure: futures have completed two rotations of a 179-point band and sit mid-band at 29,358.50, down 0.10%, with VIX below 15, oil about 1.3% lower and no cross-asset alignment behind the modest tech-specific softness. Conditional Tail holds 7 through the quietest late-Asian hours, steps to 8 for the Asian close and European cash open, and reaches 9 through the European morning and the US pre-market build, with the 12:30Z Chicago Fed National Activity Index treated as a medium-impact checkpoint at Tail 10. The US cash open inside the 13:00Z hour carries 15 for opening-auction structure, easing to 14, 12 and 11 through the US morning and lunchtime lull, then 12 for pre-event positioning. The 18:00Z hour is the peak of the series at Tail 19 and Stress 48 in event/whipsaw mode for the Treasury press conference on new Iran sanctions, with 17 for the power hour that follows; the danger window is confined to 18:00Z-20:00Z. Conditional Tail then falls to 13 at the cash close, 9 after hours and 8 across the Globex reopen and the Tuesday Asian session. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green, and confidence declines gradually from 85 to 72 with distance from the observed evidence cutoff rather than because conditions are expected to worsen.
